attempts.raw_response: The tournament featured a strong field, with world No. 1 Rafael Nadal and Serena Williams leading the respective draws. Nadal, seeking his first hard-court Masters title of the year, faced stiff competition from Novak Djokovic and Roger Federer. The women's event saw Caroline Wozniacki and Venus Williams among the top seeds. In the men's final, Andy Murray defeated Roger Federer in straight sets to claim his second Canada Masters title. On the women's side, Caroline Wozniacki triumphed over Vera Zvonareva in a three-set battle, securing her second Premier title of the season. The tournament was notable for its intense heat, which caused several player retirements, and for the strong Canadian performances, including Milos Raonic's breakthrough run to the quarterfinals.

pair.human_continuation:
It was scheduled to end August 22 but some of the matches were postponed to August 23 due to rain.

Finals

Men's singles

 Andy Murray defeated  Roger Federer, 7–5, 7–5
It was Murray's first title of the year and 15th of his career. It was his second consecutive win at the event, the first repeat Canadian Masters winner since Andre Agassi in 1994–1995.
Federer rose to world no. 2 upon reaching the final.

Women's singles

 Caroline Wozniacki defeated  Vera Zvonareva, 6–3, 6–2
It was Wozniacki's 3rd title of the year and 9th of her career. It was her first Premier 5 title.

Men's doubles

 Bob Bryan /  Mike Bryan defeated  Julien Benneteau /  Michaël Llodra, 7–5, 6–3 
 This win was the Bryan's sixteenth Masters Series win, for their careers.
pair.prefix: It was the 121st edition of the Canada Masters for the men (the 109th edition for the women), and was part of the ATP Masters Series of the 2010 ATP World Tour, and of the Premier Series of the 2010 WTA Tour. The men's event was held at the Rexall Centre in Toronto, Canada, from August 7 through August 15, 2010. The women's event was held at the Uniprix Stadium in Montreal, Canada, from August 13 through August 23, 2010.
